# ZoomInfo renewal and cancellation guide (as of 2026-11-17)

## 1. Default renewal behaviour

- **Auto-extension in at least one official version of the terms.** ZoomInfo's License Terms & Conditions dated 03/06/2024 say that 
on the date 60 days before the last day of the Term (the "Extension Date"), the Term automatically extends. The extension is for the length of the Initial Term or one year, whichever is longer, unless either party notifies the other in writing on or before the Extension Date that it should not extend.
 Treat that Extension Date as your real deadline.
- **Renewal pricing.** The same terms say the extension fee is 
the annualized Subscription Fee, plus 10% of that fee, plus any applied discount, multiplied by the length of the term in years.

- **No mid-term cancellation.** The terms state that 
the Agreement is not cancellable and remains in effect until it expires or is earlier terminated according to its terms.
 ZoomInfo's own 10-Q, as quoted by a third party, describes subscription contracts as 
typically one to three years and non-cancelable.

- **Third-party guidance agrees on 60 days.** Several recent guides report a 60-day written-notice window as typical. 
One says most ZoomInfo contracts auto-renew unless written cancellation is submitted at least 60 days before the renewal date.
 Other sources report 
notice periods of around 30–90 days depending on the contract.
 These are secondary sources, not ZoomInfo's own words.

## 2. Notice window

- **Public default:** 60 days before the last day of the term. This comes from the 2024 License Terms (see above) and is not verified against your contract.
- **Version conflict:** I found two things that don't match.
  - Two third-party reviews of the current terms say they 
set no notice period of their own, because the term is whatever the Ordering Document sets.
 One adds that 
the License Terms contain no renewal clause, and the term and any extension are set in the order form.

  - I could not retrieve the full current version of zoominfo.com/legal/ltc to settle this.
  - **Notice period in your contract: Not verified — confirm in your signed contract or with the vendor.**
- **Multi-year and negotiated deals:** One third-party source claims multi-year contracts 
commonly carry a 90-day window.
 I could not confirm this from ZoomInfo. Not verified.

## 3. Steps to give notice

1. **Find your documents.** Locate your signed Order Form and the License Terms version it references. The order form and the "Ordering Document" set your term, as the third-party reviews above note.
2. **Calculate the deadline.** Count back from the last day of your term. One third-party example: 
a term ending December 31 with a 60-day window needs written notice by November 1 at the latest.
 Build in a buffer, because 
a notice sent 59 days before the end is too late if your period is 60 days.

3. **Send written notice, not a phone call.** The terms require that the party 
notifies the other in writing.

4. **Use the contractual notice route.**
   - An archived (12/20/2021) version of the License Terms says notices 
are sent by electronic mail and deemed given when sent, with notices to ZoomInfo going
